## The claim

The alleles discovered from the reads agree with the delivered callset wherever both call, so a discordant site is a finding about one caller and not about the recovery.

**Prediction if true.** For every target gene, filter-passing calls from both read-derived callers — freebayes (Bayesian allele-frequency) and bcftools call -m (pileup) — agree with the delivered callset at at least 99% of sites where both emit a genotype. Computed after the calls exist: a concordance check, never an input to discovery.

**What would refute it.** Concordance below 99%, in which case every discordant site is listed with its evidence shot and the discovery route is re-examined before anything is concluded from it.

The weighing is a transparent heuristic for triage, not a calibrated posterior: the strengths are human judgments, and rows drawn from the same underlying data are not independent the way the sum treats them.

| 1 | proposed | — | — |
| 2 | supported | 0.88 | Supported for both callers, comfortably above the 99% line and on a large denominator: 45,512 and 43,639 co-called sites. This is the check that licenses the rest of step 2 — reads selected by k-mer bait rather than whole-genome alignment, then called by two callers of disjoint model class, reproduce the vendor pipeline's genotypes. Scope stated: single-base substitutions only, where normalisation is a no-op, so a disagreement is about the genotype and not the spelling; indels are excluded because variants_raw is layer 1 and unnormalised and its indels are not comparable without a left-alignment the query cannot do, which means the claim is untested for exactly the allele class minimap2's short-read mode is weakest at. Not held higher than 0.88 for that reason. |
